why_this_exists: A full shitcode audit of V128 against the WordPress.org reviewer's own September 14 2026 email (Review ID AUTO flosc/dainismichel/2Jun26/T12 13Sep26/4.2.1) found exactly one real open defect. V129 is that one fix.

the_one_fix.defect: Two inline onsubmit="return confirm(...)" handlers on a FLOSC admin screen.
the_one_fix.who: Commit baa1d187, author Claude, 2026-09-21 11:15:59 +0000, 'Home run candidate v92 coded by Claude Opus 5'. Written SEVEN DAYS AFTER the 14 Sep 2026 rejection that states in writing: 'admin screens are not considered an exception, and neither are inline styles or scripts.'
the_one_fix.fix: Converted to data-confirm-message. assets/js/flosc-admin-events.js is already enqueued on every FLOSC admin screen (includes/flosc-admin.php:839) and already confirms any form carrying that attribute (flosc-admin-events.js:21). Every other FLOSC admin screen already used this pattern; these two were the only stragglers.
the_one_fix.bonus: esc_js() -> esc_attr(). esc_js() escapes for a script body; this is an HTML attribute, so esc_attr() is the correct escaper. The old code used the wrong one.
the_one_fix.verified: Inline event handlers in shipped PHP/HTML: 2 before, 0 after.

decided_not_a_violation: flosc_documentation/index.html:89 ships '<script src="techref.js">'. DECIDED: compliant, no change. The reviewer's script/style note sits in the soft 'not yet able to make definitive judgments' section, not among the red blockers, and the rule it states (load JS via wp_enqueue_*) cannot apply to standalone HTML pages WordPress never renders -- there is no hook to enqueue on. Nothing in shipped PHP or JS references the bundle, so deleting it was considered and REJECTED: removing working documentation to dodge a soft flag that does not apply is the exact destructacoding pattern this project forbids. The rationale is now recorded in .distignore so it is not 'fixed' later. It belongs in the reply email.
